transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?
I’m here because elevators really scare me. I know they’re not actually dangerous, but when I have to get in one, I feel like I’m going to be trapped and I can’t make myself feel normal about it.
Does this intense fear happen only with elevators, or do you experience it in other situations as well?
It’s really elevators. I know they aren’t actually dangerous, but once I have to get in one, I get scared I’ll be trapped and I just can’t make myself feel normal about it.
How long have you been experiencing this fear of elevators?
About 11 months now. It started after we lost the house and moved into an apartment on an upper floor.

inference_history.note: Initial differential based on patient reporting intense fear of elevators and feeling trapped: specific phobia (situational/claustrophobia), agoraphobia, or panic disorder.
Patient confirmed fear is isolated to elevators and not present in other situations or occurring spontaneously, ruling out agoraphobia (F40.00) and panic disorder (F41.0).
